name: Murders
definition: Murder and non-negligent manslaughter complaints recorded by the NYPD, by the year the complaint was reported.

latest_extra.note: 204 murders reported January 1 to September 30, 2026, compared with 253 in the same span of 2025. Year-to-date file (5uac-w243) ends September 30, 2026.

source.name: NYPD Complaint Data Historic (qgea-i56i) and Current Year To Date (5uac-w243), NYC Open Data

peers.note: Murders per 100,000 residents of each city police agency's jurisdiction, from the Real-Time Crime Index historical file, which compiles FBI annual agency counts. All cities, New York included, come from that one file so they share a definition; New York's figure there (281) differs from the complaint-data series. Las Vegas is the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, whose jurisdiction includes unincorporated Clark County; Charlotte is the Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department.

source.name: Real-Time Crime Index (AH Datalytics), historical crime file based on FBI Uniform Crime Reporting data

method: SoQL count of complaints with KY_CD 101 (OFNS_DESC 'MURDER & NON-NEGL. MANSLAUGHTER'), grouped by the year of RPT_DT, the date the complaint was reported, in the historic file (2006 to December 31, 2025). The historic file ends December 31, 2025 and the year-to-date file starts January 1, 2026, so the two do not overlap and nothing is double counted. Year-to-date comparison: 2026 rows in the year-to-date file versus 2025 rows in the historic file with RPT_DT in the same January 1 to end-date window. Peers: murder_total / population x 100,000 for 2025 in the Real-Time Crime Index file, one police agency per city; each agency's population was checked against the city's Census population (within 10%, except Las Vegas and Charlotte, whose agencies cover more than the city).
caveats: These are counts of complaints in the open data, by report date. NYPD CompStat year-end murder figures are compiled separately and can differ by a few.
Counts in the open data can be revised as cases are reclassified (for example, an assault becoming a murder when a victim dies).

The FBI figures for New York, used only for the peer ranking, differ from the complaint data in these years: 2010: complaint data 535, FBI 536; 2011: complaint data 514, FBI 515; 2021: complaint data 486, FBI 488; 2023: complaint data 386, FBI 345; 2024: complaint data 382, FBI 356; 2025: complaint data 309, FBI 281. The gap is small before 2023 and larger since.
